decisions.evidence: R2 maker summarizes only that “Search and tags help you retrieve saved links quickly”; R2 client adds that search must work “regardless of capitalization.”
decisions.note: The high-level search specification omitted case-insensitive matching; the client supplied the reference behavior during goal confirmation.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker presents pasting a complete web address and clicking “Get details”; R4 client confirms that this is “the right idea.”
decisions.note: The URL-entry save flow conforms at prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker presents fetched site name, title, and description; R4 client requests that the preview “also picked up the little site icon and…a thumbnail image.”
decisions.note: The initial metadata decision omitted favicon and preview image; the client supplied both missing reference requirements.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker presents a fetched preview before commit; R4 client says she must be able to “tweak the title and the description…right there” before Save.
decisions.note: The initial preview did not provide the required pre-save editing behavior.

decisions.evidence: R5 maker presents editable fetched title/description plus favicon and thumbnail; R5 client confirms direct editing and both images are “exactly right.”
decisions.note: The revised metadata preview conforms at prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R8 maker asks whether all saving behavior checked so far matches intent; R8 client says duplicates “haven't come up yet” and expects an existing URL to open its existing bookmark for editing rather than create a copy.
decisions.note: The proposed completion of the saving flow omitted duplicate convergence; the client added it.

decisions.evidence: R9–R10 maker presents direct handoff to the existing bookmark editor and Update action; R9–R10 client confirms no fresh copy is created.
decisions.note: The revised duplicate-save flow conforms at prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R11 maker explicitly assumes search looks through only “saved titles and descriptions”; R11 client says it should eventually search “notes and the web addresses themselves” too. R12–R13 supply and confirm those searches.
decisions.note: The initial full-text field scope was incomplete; the clarification was resolved by a corrected presentation and is counted once as corrective.

decisions.evidence: R11 maker asks the client to search for uppercase “PASTA”; R11 client confirms capitalization does not prevent the match.
decisions.note: Case-insensitive search conforms at prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R12–R13 maker demonstrates matches found only in a note and URL; R12–R13 client confirms search now reaches title, description, note, and address.
decisions.note: The revised full-text field coverage conforms.

decisions.evidence: R14–R16 maker presents bookmarks carrying multiple tags, one-click tag filtering, and tag-plus-text narrowing; R14–R16 client confirms each behavior.
decisions.note: Multi-tag association and specific-tag filtering conform.

decisions.evidence: R17 maker asks whether all demonstrated tag behaviors match; R17 client says “how tags get onto a bookmark” has not been covered and requests assigning one or more during save or edit.
decisions.note: The initial tag scope covered filtering but omitted assignment.

decisions.evidence: R17 client additionally asks that typing a tag “suggest ones I've already used”; this responds to the maker’s R17 tag-area completion check.
decisions.note: Existing-tag autocomplete was missing from the initial tag scope.

decisions.evidence: R18–R23 maker presents existing-tag suggestions, multi-tag assignment, new-tag creation, and tag removal; R18–R23 client confirms the resulting behavior.
decisions.note: The revised tag-assignment flow conforms.

decisions.evidence: R24–R28 maker presents marking a bookmark for later, a dedicated Read later view, and unmarking it so it leaves that view; the client confirms all three.
decisions.note: The complete read-later lifecycle conforms.

decisions.evidence: R29 maker presents entering a personal note during saving; R29 client asks that later display preserve formatting such as bullets and bold instead of raw characters.
decisions.note: The initial note decision omitted rendered markdown behavior.

decisions.evidence: R30–R33 maker presents formatted note entry and rendered display after saving and on library cards; R30–R33 client confirms bold and bullets remain rendered.
decisions.note: The revised markdown-note behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: R34–R37 maker presents moving an item out of the active library, viewing it only in Archive, and restoring it intact; R34–R37 client confirms archive is reversible and distinct from throwing it away.
decisions.note: Archive hiding, separate archive view, and restoration conform.

decisions.evidence: After the R37 restore presentation, the R37 client says a separate permanent-delete action still needs coverage and should be confirmed because it cannot be undone.
decisions.note: The archive/restoration scope lacked the permanent alternative required to distinguish archive from delete.

decisions.evidence: R38–R42 maker presents permanent deletion, cancellation, and final removal; R38–R42 client confirms archive remains reversible while confirmed delete is final.
decisions.note: The revised delete behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: R45 establishes duplicate normalization for trailing slashes, fragments, and tracking data; R53–R54 demonstrate that an archived duplicate also opens and updates the existing item. The client confirms both cases.
decisions.note: These later duplicate decisions preserve the reference rule and cautiously extend URL equivalence.

decisions.evidence: R50–R51 maker ultimately demonstrates readable trimming with title, description, and note intact; tags are also discussed on cards elsewhere, but neither the presentations nor client responses establish that each library item exposes its favicon. R73 acceptance does not mention card favicons.
decisions.note: The long-content clarification was resolved, but evidence is insufficient to determine complete conformance of the composite list-item requirement.

decisions.evidence: R51 maker opens an existing bookmark editor with full values; R51 client confirms the full title and description remain available for editing rather than only their trimmed card previews.
decisions.note: This establishes post-save title/description editing and completes REF-BM-03.

decisions.evidence: R51 client confirms an existing editor contains title, description, and note; R9 mentions existing title/description, but no presentation or response establishes editing an existing bookmark’s URL and tags. The final review does not test those fields.
decisions.note: The record proves only part of the required edit-field set, so full divergence cannot be established.

decisions.evidence: R55 maker proposes implementing nine settled flows without opening saved links; R55 client says the basic action was never confirmed and requires clicking a bookmark to reach the original webpage.
decisions.note: The first specification gate omitted original-URL navigation.

decisions.evidence: R55 maker asks to implement the stated scope; R55 client requires ordering such as “newest first, or by title” before development begins.
decisions.note: The initial implementation scope omitted sorting.

decisions.evidence: R55 maker asks to implement the nine-flow scope; R55 client requires selecting several bookmarks and acting on them together, such as tagging or archiving a batch.
decisions.note: The initial implementation scope omitted bulk selection and actions.

decisions.evidence: R56–R57 maker demonstrates opening the saved original URL through the title or an explicit button; R57 client selects the clickable-title version after confirming both open the original page.
decisions.note: The revised original-page navigation conforms; the two UI choices were functionally equivalent.

decisions.evidence: R58–R61 maker presents newest-first and title ordering, including sorting within filtered results; R58–R61 client confirms the behavior.
decisions.note: The revised sort behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: R62 maker’s batch bar initially offers only “Add tags” and “Archive selected”; R62 client says it must also cover read-later/done and deleting a selection.
decisions.note: The first bulk-action presentation supported selection but omitted several required action types.

decisions.evidence: R71 maker’s claimed complete batch range lists adding a tag, read-later/done, archive, and delete, but no removal of tags; R71 client says this is the “whole” bulk experience without identifying that omission. R73 implementation review again mentions only bulk tag addition.
decisions.note: The revised batch scope still omits bulk tag removal. The approval is bare with respect to that reference difference.

decisions.evidence: R72 maker characterizes the settled feature as “managing selected bookmarks in batches”; the demonstrated operations act on explicitly selected items, and no presentation offers applying an action directly to the whole collection matching the current filter. R72 client approves the scope without surfacing that difference.
decisions.note: The final specification gate uses a selected-item bulk model and omits the whole-current-filter action.

decisions.evidence: R72 maker closes the specification after search flows limited to field substrings and sidebar tag filtering; no `#tag` query syntax was presented. R72 client approves “searching across everything” without identifying the syntax gap.
decisions.note: The final search scope omits reference-required hashtag syntax; general approval does not show awareness.

decisions.evidence: R72 maker declares all feature flows settled, but the prior search presentations contain no AND/OR/NOT operators, parentheses, or literal-operator quoting rule. R72 client approves without mentioning them.
decisions.note: Boolean and grouped query behavior is absent from the approved scope.

decisions.evidence: R72 maker declares the search scope settled without any quoted exact-phrase behavior; R72 client’s approval does not express that difference.
decisions.note: Exact quoted-phrase search is omitted at the final specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R72 maker closes the exhaustive twelve-flow scope without local page snapshots or the PDF-download rule; R72 client approves the listed scope, and R73 implementation review does not surface the omission.
decisions.note: Local HTML/PDF preservation is absent from the approved and reviewed implementation scope.

decisions.evidence: R72 maker closes the exhaustive feature scope without Internet Archive snapshot creation; R72–R73 client approval never identifies that difference.
decisions.note: Internet Archive snapshot support is silently omitted.

decisions.evidence: R73 maker presents the application as complete; R73 client explicitly says that in a future round she “might like…saving a favorite search as a reusable view,” while stating it is “not part of what we agreed this time” and accepting completion.
decisions.note: At implementation review the client surfaces the missing saved-search/bundle concept and explicitly accepts its deferral.

decisions.evidence: R73 client explicitly identifies “bringing bookmarks in…from my browser” as a future convenience, says it is outside the current agreement, and accepts the completed app.
decisions.note: The client surfaces import as missing and explicitly accepts the departure for this cycle.

decisions.evidence: R73 client explicitly identifies bringing bookmarks “out to my browser” as future work, says it is not part of the current agreement, and accepts completion.
decisions.note: The client surfaces export as missing and explicitly accepts the departure for this cycle.

decisions.evidence: R72 maker closes the scope with a transient ordering control but no personal settings for default sort, displayed-item count, or font size; R72–R73 client accepts without identifying this difference.
decisions.note: Display-related user settings are omitted; approving the application does not establish awareness of the omission.
